title: Detecting and Mitigating Subliminal Bias Transmission in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
summary: This paper proposes a method to detect and mitigate subliminal transmission of harmful traits (e.g., political bias) in multi-agent LLM systems. We introduce a framework that uses mechanistic interpretability to identify neuron populations responsible for bias amplification, then applies targeted weight regularization during training. The approach is validated on a political bias benchmark, measuring bias intensity before/after mitigation and comparing against baselines like adversarial training. The method is supported by evidence of subliminal learning in LLM agents and the need for bias control in educational systems.
gap: Current multi-agent LLM systems (e.g., FACET) lack mechanisms to detect and prevent subliminal transmission of harmful traits through training data or agent interactions, despite evidence of such risks in LLM-based content generation.
approach: 1) Use mechanistic analysis to identify neurons correlated with bias traits 2) Apply layer-specific weight regularization during training 3) Implement a monitoring agent to detect bias drift in generated content 4) Test on a political bias benchmark with GPT-2 and FACET-like systems
evaluation: Baselines: standard training, adversarial debiasing, data filtering. Measures: bias intensity score (0-1), model performance (accuracy), neuron activation patterns. Comparison against [ref-004]'s original FACET system and [ref-010]'s bias amplification results.
